title: Veterans' Group Life Insurance (VGLI) Policy Conditions: Unpaid Premiums, Lapse and Reinstatement
content:
# Veterans' Group Life Insurance (VGLI) Policy Conditions: Unpaid Premiums, Lapse and Reinstatement

## Conditions

**1. Grace period.** A premium not received by its due date starts a grace period of 60 days, during which coverage stays in force. The days of the grace period are counted as calendar days of coverage with no premium paid covering them, from the day after the paid-to date (the last day of paid coverage) through the current date.

**2. Lapse warning.** A lapse warning is sent 30 days after the due date.

**3. Cure.** Paying the overdue premium within the grace period keeps the policy active.

**4. Lapse.** Otherwise coverage lapses at the end of the paid period. The lapse date is the paid-to date.

**5. Reinstatement.** A lapsed policy can be reinstated within 5 years by paying all premiums from the lapse date and showing good health; every Veterans' Group Life Insurance (VGLI) tier requires both the back premiums and proof of good health for reinstatement.

## Policy status through these conditions

| From | To | When |
|---|---|---|
| active | grace | a premium is unpaid on its due date and the grace period begins |
| grace | active | the overdue premium is paid within the grace period |
| grace | lapsed | the grace period ends without payment and coverage ends |
| lapsed | active | the lapsed policy is reinstated after back premiums are paid and the required health evidence is accepted |

While the status is grace, coverage is in force.

## Timeline (hypothetical policy)

*Hypothetical inputs: a monthly-billed policy paid to 31 March; the premium due 1 April is not received on its due date.*

```
31 Mar   paid-to date (last day of paid coverage)
 1 Apr   due date passes unpaid — grace period begins; unpaid day 1
 1 May   30 days after the due date — lapse warning sent
30 May   unpaid day 60 — last day of the 60-day grace period
```

- **Paid on 20 May** (unpaid day 50): the overdue premium is paid within the grace period, and the policy stays active.
- **Not paid during the grace period**: coverage lapses at the end of the paid period; the lapse date recorded is 31 March.
- **Reinstatement two years later** (hypothetical): the lapsed policy is within the 5-year window; reinstating it takes payment of all premiums from the 31 March lapse date and proof of good health.

## Basis questions

- *Is the insured covered while a premium is overdue but the grace period is still running?* Yes. Coverage stays in force during the grace period.
- *From what date does a lapsed policy's coverage end?* At the end of the paid period — the paid-to date.
- *To reinstate, does the insured pay only the premium that was missed first?* No. Reinstatement takes all premiums from the lapse date, together with proof of good health.
